name: 5410 BC Solar Proton Event

phenomena.details: Single-year Delta-14C rise of ~6 per mil over 5411-5410 BCE in three Northern Hemisphere tree-ring chronologies; smaller than AD 775.

impacts.description: Moderate-to-strong solar energetic particle event producing a measurable single-year enhancement in atmospheric radiocarbon.
Prehistoric event known only from cosmogenic radiocarbon in tree rings.

papers.title: A single-year cosmic ray event at 5410 BCE registered in 14C of tree rings
papers.authors: Miyake, F., Panyushkina, I. P., Jull, A. J. T., et al.
papers.keyFinding: Detected a ~6 per mil single-year radiocarbon increase at 5410 BCE in bristlecone pine (USA), larch (Switzerland) and Scots pine (Finland), with a 14C signature matching confirmed solar particle events.

summary: A single-year extreme solar particle event in 5410 BC, recorded as a ~6 per mil radiocarbon increase in three Northern Hemisphere tree-ring chronologies - genuine but more moderate than the AD 774 event.
description: Miyake et al. (2021) identified a single-year radiocarbon increase of about 6 per mil spanning 5411-5410 BCE in three independent, widely separated Northern Hemisphere chronologies: Californian bristlecone pine, Swiss larch and Finnish Scots pine. The synchronous, single-year form of the signal matches the confirmed solar energetic particle events (AD 774/775, AD 993/994, ~660 BC), supporting a solar origin, although no ice-core 10Be/36Cl confirmation was presented. At roughly half the amplitude of AD 775 (~12 per mil), it is a genuine but more moderate event, useful both as an additional data point on the frequency of extreme solar storms and as a dendrochronological tie-point.
